From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: SDK / Auth / Routing action items + fallback map for HelioHealth

Hi Maya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a clear plan for integration and the routing/policy design we discussed.

Recap (short):
- Goal: integrate Redwood inference into HelioHealth's triage flow for patient intake summaries and question answering. Will need streaming chat, structured tool-calling for a summarizer service, and embeddings + reranker for search.
- Constraints you flagged: tight 300ms P99 for triage micro-interactions (US region), PHI scope (we discussed Private VPC), and procurement timeline end of quarter.

Action items I’m proposing (owner / eta):
1) SDK & auth pilot: provide a drop-in Node + Python quickstart that shows SDK + OAuth2 + mutual TLS example (owner: me) — target: 2027-10-06
2) Sandbox access: grant Helio sandbox API key + VPC peering instructions so you can smoke-test routing and KV-caching (owner: Markus) — target: 2027-10-07
3) Routing & fallback map: propose a primary low-latency model + warm fallback stack for heavy requests that exceed token limits or for cost optimization (owner: Chloe) — draft by 2027-10-08
4) Embeddings/reranker sample: small eval using a subset of your search queries to compare single-stage vs. hybrid rerank (owner: me/you) — initial numbers due 2027-10-11

Technical notes for the routing/fallback map (high-level):
- Primary: low-latency quantized model (gpus in us-west) pinned for triage with strict 300ms P99 SLO.
- Warm fallback: when queue depth > 8 or model warms exceed configured KV window, route to a slightly larger model in the same region (adds 60-120ms) with reduced max tokens.
- Cold fallback / cost-optimized path: if cost budget threshold is hit or US region capacity constrained, route to a cheaper, multi-tenant hosted variant in a different region with same safety filters.
- Tool-calling: structured output schema enforced at the API layer; prefer function-call semantics over free-text parsers for the summarizer (we’ll include example function schema).

Attachments I’m including: redwood-sdk-quickstart.patch (small example changes for your devs), auth-config-example.yaml (mTLS / OAuth snippet), helio-sandbox-access.txt (sandbox URL + expiration).

Next steps: confirm who should get sandbox access, and whether Procurement needs the standard SOW + security addendum now or later. If you’re good with the action items I’ll push the quickstart and invite your engs to the sandbox tomorrow.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Maya / Samir — added Samir and Procurement per your note. Quick answers inline and next uploads: 

1) SLO measurement: Redwood will provide both a model-inference measurement (service-side token latency) and an end-to-end SDK-measured timing (we’ll instrument the SDK to emit a timing header). For contract SLOs we typically use the SDK-measured P95/P99 as the observable; we can add synthetic checks from your side as well.

2) Sandbox: Markus will send a sandbox invite and the VPC peering doc (expect email from markus_klein@redwood.com). Sandbox credentials expire in 14 days; we’ll provide a README with smoke tests that exercise routing decisions and KV cache hits.

3) Audit logs: attached sample export (auth-config-example.yaml includes the control-plane retention example). For Private deployment, customer-managed logs are available via the connectors described in section 3 of the drive spec: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-helio-arch-spec

Routing/fallback specifics (concrete proposal):
- Route key: session_type + payload_size + latency_slo_hint. This lets your frontend tag triage vs. long-form generation.
- Policy rules (example):
  * If latency_slo_hint == "strict" and region == US -> route to q4_300ms (pinned)
  * Else if queue_depth > 8 -> route to q6_warm (same region) with max_tokens=256
  * Else if cost_threshold_burn_rate > 0.8 -> route to shared-hosted-lowcost (fallback, different region)
- Embeddings/reranker: recommend a two-stage approach for your search traffic: dense embeddings (128-d) for recall -> light-weight transformer reranker for top-50. We can provide a sample pipeline comparing latency & accuracy trade-offs.

I’ve attached the SDK patch and auth snippet. Markus — can you send the sandbox link and peering instructions after this thread? Chloe — can you draft the fallback map visual (simple table + flow) and share by EOD 10/08?

Best,
Diego

Attachments referenced: auth-config-example.yaml, redwood-sdk-quickstart.patch

Hi all — I put together a short fallback map and a table mapping policy triggers to routing targets. See summary below and I’ve uploaded a quick diagram to the Drive link (see related_links).

Summary (Chloe):
- Hot path (300ms P99 target): q4_300ms (pinned, us-west) — use continuous batching with KV cache window 4s.
- Warm path: q6_warm (same region) — aggressive token limit reduction, allow service-level batching window 20ms.
- Cold/cost path: shared-hosted-lowcost (us-east) — apply extra safety/post-processing to match safety filters.
- Tool-calling: prefer function schema with explicit fields: {action: summarize, patient_id, redact_pii:true}. We will provide JSON schema & example.

Open question for Helio: are you comfortable with a secondary region failover for non-PII workloads only, or do you want PHI to strictly stay in-region? We flagged this as a policy decision that affects capacity planning.

I’ll follow up with the diagram and table link.

Chloe
Chloe Martin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
